guideTitle: Best Ceiling Medallions for Living Rooms (2026)
metaTitle: Best Ceiling Medallions for Living Rooms (2026)
metaDescription: We evaluated six ceiling medallions by diameter, canopy fit, material and projection, with picks for pendants, ceiling fans and formal chandeliers.
expertTake: The 13 inch EIFHYT is our top pick for its balanced size, hardware and two-pack. The Westinghouse is the value pick for small fixtures at the lowest cost. Anyone whose fixture canopy already sits neatly on a clean ceiling should skip the category.
introParagraphs: A ceiling medallion is trim, not a fixture. Its job is to frame the canopy of a pendant, chandelier or ceiling fan and to hide the rough hole and paint damage that installers leave behind.
The key choices are diameter, centre hole and material. A medallion that is too large looks heavy, one that is too small does not cover the damage, and one with the wrong hole size leaves a gap.

products.name: EIFHYT 13 Inch Polyurethane Ceiling Medallion, 2 Pack with Hardware
products.description:
The 13 inch EIFHYT is the most useful size in the lineup because it suits the fixtures most living rooms actually have. The listing says it works best with medium lamps below 42 inches across, such as pendants and small chandeliers, and it comes as a pair, which covers a second fixture or a mistake. The material is a polyurethane foam that is lightweight and carries a smooth, paintable surface.

At only 3/4 inch of projection it is shallow, so the relief is subtle and it reads as a gentle ring around the canopy. Against the 18 inch EIFHYT it is far less dramatic, but it is also far less likely to look oversized. Against the 10 inch ELFCAB nylon pair, it covers a bigger patch of damaged paint. The hardware pack lists a threaded pipe, screws and anchors, which means you can mount a light fixture through it.

Installation is simple: switch off the power at the breaker, remove the canopy, thread the wiring through the centre hole, fasten the medallion with adhesive or screws, and refit the canopy over it. Paint it to match the ceiling with a brush before hanging if you want it to disappear. Foam dents under a fingernail, so handle the edges gently.
products.bestFor: Medium pendants and small chandeliers where a modest, paintable ring is wanted.
pros: Thirteen inch size suits pendants and small chandeliers under 42 inches across
Two-pack covers a second room or a spare for painting mistakes
Mounting hardware is included, so you can fit it without separate purchases
Lightweight polyurethane takes paint evenly and mounts easily to a ceiling
cons: Only 3/4 inch of projection gives a subtle look that suits flatter ceilings
Foam surface dents and marks with fingernails or tools, so handle with care

products.name: EIFHYT 18 Inch Primed Urethane Ceiling Medallion, 4 Inch ID, 2 Pack
products.description:
The 18 inch model is the one for ceiling fans and big pendants. The listing says it suits a 52 inch fan with a 7-1/2 inch canopy, and its 4 inch centre hole is large enough to take a fan's downrod hardware. It arrives primed, so you only need to paint it to match, and it comes as a pair.

At 18 inches across and 1-1/8 inches deep it is the most visible medallion here besides the 22 inch Ekena. It costs more than the 13 inch EIFHYT because of the size, and it only looks right when the fixture is large enough to justify it. A small pendant over a big medallion looks lost, which is the classic sizing mistake.

Because it is lightweight urethane, it mounts with adhesive and a few screws into joists or blocking, not into plaster alone. Fit the medallion before hanging the fan, and check that the fan blades clear its edge by a safe margin. Primed urethane shows seams if the join is not caulked, so fill them and paint twice.
products.bestFor: Ceiling fans and large chandeliers in rooms with a ceiling high enough to carry a bold ring.
pros: Eighteen inch size gives a proper ring behind a 52 inch fan canopy
Arrives primed, so only a finish coat is needed to match the ceiling
Four inch centre hole accommodates the fan's mounting hardware easily
Two-pack allows a second fan or a spare in case of damage
cons: Looks oversized with a small fixture, which is the common sizing mistake
Costs more than the smaller medallions and needs a solid fixing point

products.name: Ekena Millwork 22 Inch Traditional Thermoformed PVC Ceiling Medallion
products.description:
The Ekena is the largest and deepest medallion here at 22 inches across and 1-1/2 inches of projection. It is made from thermoformed PVC, which the maker describes as moisture resistant and not prone to cracking or warping, and it fits canopies up to 13-1/2 inches. The pattern is traditional, with layered rings that suit formal or classic rooms.

Size is the question. A 22 inch medallion needs a fixture that can hold its own, such as a large chandelier or a fan with a wide canopy, and a ceiling high enough that the piece does not crowd. It costs more than the 13 inch pair and much more than the smaller ones. The listing notes multiple sizes and finishes of the same design, so you can step down if 22 inches proves too much.

PVC is an advantage in a humid space, since it does not swell the way wood or plaster can. It paints well with a bonding primer. Because the piece is thin-walled, back it with adhesive over its whole rim, and let it set before you hang a heavy fixture.
products.bestFor: Large chandeliers and formal rooms that want a bold, traditional ceiling feature.
pros: Twenty-two inch size gives the most presence of any medallion in this guide
Thermoformed PVC resists moisture and does not warp like wood or plaster
Fits canopies up to 13-1/2 inches, so it suits wide fixtures
Available in several sizes and finishes in the same design
cons: Size overwhelms small fixtures and low ceilings, which makes it easy to get wrong
Costs more than most of the other medallions here for a single piece

products.name: Crapyt 12 Inch Carved Polyurethane Ceiling Medallion, 3.35 Inch ID
products.description:
The Crapyt offers the most detailed pattern for its size, with relief carvings and fine textures that give it a vintage look. It measures 12.01 inches across with a 3.35 inch centre hole, and it mounts with adhesive in minutes without drilling, according to the listing. The polyurethane keeps the weight low.

It is an easy choice for a light fixture in a rented space where drilling is not welcome, though adhesive alone is only sensible for a light piece. Against the EIFHYT 13 inch it offers more pattern and less size, and it is cheaper. Check that your canopy is bigger than the 3.35 inch hole and smaller than the outer diameter, since the canopy has to cover the hole while sitting inside the ring.

Dust gathers in the relief, so run a soft brush around it on cleaning day. Paint it with a thin coat so the carving does not clog. Test the adhesive on an inconspicuous patch if the ceiling has a textured finish.
products.bestFor: Light fixtures in rooms that want detailed ornament without drilling.
pros: Carved relief gives more visual interest than the plain rings here
Adhesive mounting needs no drilling, which suits renters or fragile ceilings
Twelve inch size suits small pendants and semi-flush fixtures
Costs less than the 13 inch EIFHYT pair for a single decorative piece
cons: Adhesive-only mounting suits light fixtures but not heavy ones
Detail traps dust and can clog under thick paint, so use thin coats

products.name: ELFCAB 10 Inch White Molded Nylon Ceiling Medallion, 4 Inch ID, 2 Pack
products.description:
The ELFCAB is a small, tough ring for small fixtures. At 10 inches across it suits lamps of 23 inches or smaller, such as mini pendants and semi-flush lights, according to the listing. The material is molded nylon, a rigid plastic that resists denting and keeps its shape better than foam.

Nylon is heavier than foam but more durable, and the white finish can be painted. The pair costs little, and the smaller size is the right call when a larger medallion would crowd the fixture. A plain ring will not impress as ornament, but it does hide the rough hole and uneven paint around a canopy, which is the real job for most buyers.

Check that the canopy is larger than the 4 inch centre hole, or the hole will show. Fit and trim before you paint. Because nylon does not absorb paint like urethane, use a bonding primer.
products.bestFor: Small pendants and semi-flush fixtures where the aim is to hide a rough patch.
pros: Rigid molded nylon keeps its shape and resists dents better than foam
Ten inch size suits small fixtures without overwhelming them
Pair pack lets you do two fixtures or keep a spare
Costs little for a practical fix to damaged paint around a canopy
cons: Plain design offers little ornament, so it works as a cover and not decor
Needs bonding primer before paint, since nylon does not take paint like urethane

products.name: Westinghouse 7702700 Victorian Ceiling Medallion, 10 Inch, White
products.description:
The Westinghouse is the lightest and lowest cost option here at 0.32 pounds and a single piece. It has a Victorian pattern and a white finish, and the listing says it was made in the United States. At 10 inches in diameter it suits small fixtures.

Light weight means it can be stuck up with adhesive, though only on a clean, flat ceiling. It lacks the mounting hardware of the EIFHYT 13 inch pair, so you buy fixings separately if the fixture needs them. Against the ELFCAB nylon pair, it offers a decorative pattern where the nylon is plain.

Because the listing gives little detail about the material, treat it as a light decorative piece and not a structural one. Paint it, test the fit around your canopy and check the centre opening against your fixture before fixing. Keep it away from steam, since many lightweight mouldings soften in damp.
products.bestFor: Small fixtures and tight budgets where a simple Victorian pattern is wanted.
pros: Lowest cost in the lineup makes it an easy, low-risk purchase
Victorian pattern adds more character than the plain nylon rings
At 0.32 pounds it hangs with adhesive on a clean ceiling
Listed as made in the United States, which some buyers prefer
cons: Listing gives little detail on material, so durability is less clear
No mounting hardware is described, so you may need to buy fixings

buyingCriteria.explanation: A common rule of thumb is a medallion between one third and one half of the fixture's width, and always larger than the canopy. The 13 inch EIFHYT suits fixtures below 42 inches wide, the 10 inch ELFCAB suits lamps of 23 inches or smaller, and the 18 inch EIFHYT suits a 52 inch fan. Buying too large is the most common mistake and is hard to fix after painting.

The medallion's inner diameter must be smaller than the fixture's canopy, so the canopy hides the hole, and its outer diameter must be larger than the canopy. The Ekena lists a 3-1/2 inch hole and fits canopies up to 13-1/2 inches. Measure the canopy, not the fixture, and write it down.

Polyurethane foam, as on the EIFHYT 13 inch, is light and paintable but dents. Nylon, as on the ELFCAB, is rigid and heavier. PVC, as on the Ekena, resists moisture. Weight matters for fixing, since a light piece can be adhered and a heavy one needs screws into framing.

Projection is how far the ring stands off the ceiling. The EIFHYT 13 inch lists 3/4 inch, the Ekena 1-1/2 inches. Shallow suits flat modern ceilings, deep suits traditional rooms with crown moulding. A deep medallion with a flush-mount fixture can leave a gap.

Primed urethane, like the 18 inch EIFHYT, is ready to paint. A white nylon piece needs a bonding primer. Painting a medallion to match the ceiling makes it look built in. Use a brush and thin coats to keep detail crisp.

Switch off the power at the breaker before removing a canopy. Light medallions can be glued, but a fan or heavy chandelier must hang from the electrical box and structure, never from the medallion. If you are unsure about wiring, hire an electrician.

specDecoder.watchFor: The lineup runs from 10 inches on the Westinghouse and ELFCAB to 22 inches on the Ekena.

specDecoder.meaning: The centre hole that wiring passes through, which the canopy must cover.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EIFHYT 13 inch lists 3.5 inches while the 18 inch lists 4 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: How far the medallion stands out from the ceiling.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Ekena lists 1-1/2 inches, so check that your canopy can sit flat against it.

specDecoder.meaning: The largest canopy diameter the medallion is designed to sit behind.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Ekena lists up to 13-1/2 inches, and the EIFHYT 13 inch is rated for lamps below 42 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: A base coat that makes the surface ready for paint.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 18 inch EIFHYT is primed, while the nylon pieces need a bonding primer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Specification review
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each medallion from its published dimensions, material and fitting details. Sizes ranged from 10 inches to 22 inches across.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fixture matching
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each size to the fixtures it suits, using the maker's guidance, such as lamps below 42 inches for the 13 inch pair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read patterns in owner feedback for recurring problems: poor fit around canopies, warped edges, paint adhesion and missing hardware. We weighted repeated themes over single comments.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and finish assessment
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared polyurethane, nylon and PVC for weight, paintability and moisture resistance. Scores are editorial assessments, not measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We favoured pieces that include hardware or clear instructions and that can be fitted by a careful home owner.

cards.label: Foam (EIFHYT, Crapyt)
cards.text: Light, paintable and easy to fit with adhesive. Dents and shows seams if not filled.

cards.label: Rigid (ELFCAB nylon, Ekena PVC)
cards.text: Keeps its shape and resists damp. Heavier and needs a bonding primer.

howToChoose.note: Choose foam for light fixtures and clean paint jobs, and rigid plastic for humid rooms or hard use.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A diameter in proportion to the fixture, a finish you can paint to match the ceiling and a canopy fit that hides the centre hole.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EIFHYT 13 inch suits most living room pendants. The 18 inch and Ekena suit a fan or a grand chandelier.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The fixture is large, the room is formal or the medallion will be a visible feature. The Ekena and 18 inch EIFHYT suit that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You are covering a rough patch around a small fixture. The ELFCAB and Westinghouse do that for little.

maintenance.why: Dust settles in carved detail and shows against white. A soft brush clears it.
Heat from a fixture and humidity weaken adhesive. Re-fix any lifting edge.
Chips show against a painted ceiling. Use a small brush and matching paint.
A gap between canopy and medallion shows the hole. Tighten the canopy screws.
Heat and light can yellow plastics. Repaint with a suitable primer if needed.

faq.q: What size ceiling medallion do I need?
faq.a: Pick a diameter between a third and a half of your fixture's width, and make sure the canopy covers the centre hole. The 13 inch EIFHYT suits fixtures below 42 inches, and the 18 inch suits a 52 inch fan.

faq.q: What is the best budget ceiling medallion?
faq.a: The Westinghouse is the lowest cost here. The ELFCAB nylon two-pack is a close second and gives a more rigid ring.

faq.q: Can I paint a ceiling medallion?
faq.a: Yes. Primed urethane takes paint directly, and nylon needs a bonding primer. Use thin coats to keep detail crisp.

faq.q: Do medallions hold a heavy fixture?
faq.a: No. A fixture must hang from the electrical box and ceiling structure. The medallion is trim only.
Switch off the power, remove the canopy, thread the wiring through, fix the medallion with adhesive or screws and refit the canopy over it. If you are unsure, hire an electrician.

faq.q: Will it work with a ceiling fan?
faq.a: Yes, with a large enough diameter and centre hole, such as the 18 inch EIFHYT. Make sure the blades clear the medallion.
